summary:
# NOTES: Blue-Stocking Hall (Scargill, William Pitt; 1827, Henry Colburn, 3 vols)

Source header says 3 Gutenberg vols merged (IDs 40974, 52375, 55407). Text has VOL. I, VOL. II, VOL. III headings. Epigraph: Love's Labour Lost "From woman's eyes this doctrine I derive..." Printer: J. B. Nichols, 25 Parliament Street. Preface: "Gentle Reader"; author claims motive is recantation of prejudice against "Bas Bleus."

Framing: Epistolary novel of letters among a circle. Narrator/letter-writer chiefly ARTHUR HOWARD, a fashionable young man (of Selby, Buckinghamshire; Grosvenor Square London; Cambridge) who visits Irish cousins at Glenalta, county Kerry, and reforms from prejudice against "Blue-stockings" (learned women). Journals are later tidied for "Gentle Reader"; Howard's final letter (XLVI) addresses the reader, says he is a "penitent convert", and that the Douglas family is the model of learned-yet-feminine women.

## VOL. I (Letters I–XI)

**Letter I** – Charles Falkland (Cambridge friend of Howard) to Arthur Howard, written at Dover before sailing to Calais, bound for Geneva. Mentions "treaty ratified at Cambridge on Monday evening". Falkland's mother was his "Gamaliel", died when he was 16 (he lost her at sixteen; "orphan," guardian "excellent man" who condoled). Falkland believes his fate is linked with the Douglas family of Glenalta, Kerry; calls it "Quixotism"; compares to Mahomet's pilgrims to Mecca; cites Falstaff "God help the wicked." Howard's aunt and cousins at Glenalta; Howard assigned to write journals.

**Letter II** – Emily Douglas to Julia Sandford (Glenalta). Mr. Otway (neighbour, "Phil.") was ill three months; family nursed him, ran his schools, visited poor. Frederick is Emily's brother; Charlotte, Fanny (sisters). Expect Cousin Arthur Howard, delicate lungs, son of Mrs. Howard (Aunt, Buckinghamshire, "Island of mists" Ireland). Arthur is only son; accompanied to Glenalta in place of Falkland's Continent trip. Emily mentions a "little solitary spot" (the Retreat), to be told in next letter. Emily's mother = Mrs. Douglas (Caroline). Frederick is referred to as "Frederick" and called "pill-garlicks" on family labor.

**Letter III** – Arthur Howard to Falkland, from Glenalta. Journey across bog (Kerry). Arrived at six o'clock previous evening; post-chaise, Lewis is his valet/servant ("Lewis had descended"). Aunt, a sweet-voiced lady, sends him to rooms, asks Frederick to show him. Howard finds library full of "Blues": Sallust, Virgil, Sowerby on Minerals, botany books, initials E. and C. Douglas. Fanny (≈15, pretty, "funny" face) is "sheet anchor". Dinner: good food; no brogue. Fred is sportsman (greyhounds, setters). Evening: Emily writing music, Charlotte tuning harp, Fanny rolling ball for spaniel; they sing Irish airs; a quadrille dance. At ten a tray of fruit, milk. Then family prayers with six servants and old Lawrence (grey-haired, stick, cushion placed by Fanny); a chapter from New Testament. Howard plans to leave quickly. Mentions Marmontel, Agathe, "La plus jolie espiègle…"; Solon; Latin "Hic hæc hoc"; Selecta.

**Letter IV** – Mrs. Douglas (Caroline) to Mrs. E. Sandford (Elizabeth, Checkley, Derbyshire). Caroline's children "doubly orphaned". Sandfords expected at Glenalta in August. Caroline's sorrows: during fever at cottage near Linton, Devonshire, Frederick (then 12) left a poem "To my beloved Mamma" ("And wilt thou also fall asleep?") which revived her. Tutor Mr. Oliphant (old, religious, benevolent; procured by Edward Otway; at Lisfarne). Mrs. Barbauld's advice on education quoted ("moral atmosphere" is the real teacher). Caroline on her children; Arthur's situation: his mother's "silly society"; Emily reasons with Arthur, Charlotte expostulates, Fanny banters. Oliphant returns from northern trip "next week."

**Letter V** – Arthur to Falkland (long, Glenalta, May morning). Lewis reports family up early. Fanny brings milk from Drimindhu (favourite cow) for Arthur's cough; Fanny says Lorry (old Lawrence) is her "mother's foster-father" (husband of mamma's nurse Nanny). Frederick and sisters return from donkeys; Louisa and Adelaide (Arthur's sisters) live in town. Frederick says prayers are optional for Arthur (valet Lewis attends). Caroline described by Arthur ("heavenly looking being," about forty, widow's weeds). Otway (Phil.) arrives ~ 55 years old, tall, fine teeth, shaggy cloak, staff. Caroline sets schedule: luncheon at two. Walk with Emily and Frederick: Lisfarne Wood, the bay; Emily's apology about Otway ("Is he one of aunt's aspirants?" offends Emily; she weeps; forgiven). Eileen (barefoot peasant, husband Jem ill, priest Father Clancy, flax, "Miss Emly"). Fanny and butterflies / grubs. Luncheon; Iceland moss. Evening: discussion on blue-stockings; Fanny asks why "Blue-stockings" term; Otway says term is slang for learned ladies; Mr. Stillingfleet and Mrs. Montagu's soirées; Otway says women "contemned as rivals", men "avoided as bores"; Fanny cries, calls him "Phil." (short for philosopher, given by her, "Encyclopedia"). Otway's arguments on education; Arthur argues women should leave reading to men; Otway replies at length (accomplishments as acanthus, fashionable education, theatre and actresses marriage, "Woman's empire ... Home"; Ariosto's blue and gold quote). Arthur mentions Drury Lane, Covent Garden. Mentions Mr. Bentley arriving; George Bentley (Bentley nephew; blushes at Charlotte's name). Arthur calls the Douglas family "Blue-stockings without pedantry."

**Letter VI** – Arthur to Falkland (Lisfarne, breakfast with Otway). Emily's narration of Otway's life: schoolmates Pylades/Orestes with Emily's father Henry Douglas; Caroline and Henry poor-engaged, Otway guardian of secret. Otway once loved "Stella" (Mrs. Stanhope), who married wealthy Mr. Stanhope and later a young fortune-hunter; Stanhope's son (young Stanhope, Otway's ward, age 14 then) ; Otway went to London (Mr. Scriven's, solicitor); Mrs. Stanhope fled to Continent, died about two years earlier; Otway's poem "On first seeing Stella in a coloured dress after her second marriage" (quoted; footnote Cactus Grandiflora). Otway's house: Lisfarne purchased; Glenalta purchased for Douglas family. Emily's cabin visit to Susan Lambert (sick woman; children Tommy, Nancy; baby). Emily makes gruel, lights fire; Arthur fetches heath. Lisfarne: Otway's breakfast with dogs (Newfoundland), tortoise-shell cat, peafowl. Otway's library: novels in "Poets' Corner"; Byron debate; Arthur defends Byron; Otway opposes. Otway's paddock of old horses; "Pastime Row" of cottages; Kate Sullivan ("Queen of Pastime Row"; blind; pony True-penny; holy well). Otway's schools: industry school and reading school with penny per week; Bible; priests oppose Bible. Visit to cave/bower sacred to Henry Douglas (uncle, "Corinthian pillar"); Heu quanto minus epitaph (Leasowes). Caroline's marriage recalled ("they were formed for each other"). Otway's botanic garden; plan to send plants to Fanny. Otway's long argument on female education and utility; Bentley arrives for dinner. Tutor Oliphant (Domine) arrives; Imprimis: no wig, bald pate. Library gifts for family from Otway (Clarke's Bible for aunt, Flora Londinensis, Biographical Dictionary, Herodotus, Withering's Botany for Fanny; Scott novels). Glenalta furnishing described. Clothing of cousins described.

**Letter VII** – Arthur to Falkland (Glenalta, Sunday). Walk with aunt; Arthur advises against educating daughters ("marriage" argument); Caroline replies with views on marriage; the barrister and wife story; diplomat's wife story; Oliphant arrives with Charlotte and Fanny at moss-house; Caroline bids them send "little car". Oliphant and Arthur debate women and Scripture (Eve, "she-man", Ishau; Sarah; Mary; Woman first witness of resurrection). Oliphant on Solomon finding no good woman. Arthur on Rights of Women book. Sunday school: Emily, Charlotte, Fanny teach before breakfast. Church at parish, bleak; Mr. Leighton (preacher, tall, thin, pale; sermon on prayer). Calvinism debate (Bentley, Oliphant). Fanny distributes bread and money; Tim (wife dead six years). Arthur reflects on society: "society consists in number of ideas" (Falkland's remark). Killarney planned for July.

Also in VII: Caroline's secret; Emily's proposal to visit Killarney; the family's petition; Fanny's frog; Oliphant (domestic chaplain). Caroline thanks Arthur; Arthur cries at the children's scheme.

**Letter VIII** – Emily to Julia Sandford. Surprise for mother: "the Retreat" (hidden glen). Discovery years earlier: beech tree with initials H. A. C. D. (Henry, Caroline Douglas); verse found tied to pencil, in mamma's hand ("Inscribed upon thy polished rind"). Tom Collins (peasant), son Darby died; Tom's midsummer prayer story (Caroline praying at beech tree). Temple built: reed-matting, elm pillars, pebble paving, alabaster urn from Pompeii (father's), lines engraved ("Bless'd refuge of a sad and broken heart"), stained-glass window, Kerry marble slab, pocket Bible inscribed "The prayer of the righteous availeth much." Tom's cabin improved. Caroline visits (with Frederick, Emily); emotion; Tom weeps. Old Andrew on "good men and good books." Arthur's changes; Killarney trip planned; Arthur "enthusiast"; Emily as "Linnaea."

**Letter IX** – Charles Falkland to Arthur Howard, from Rome. Falkland with Richard Oliphant (Domine's nephew) and young Stanhope, at Rome. Discusses French vs English conversation ("pints of water chucked into a pump"). Mentions Madame du Deffand. Falkland urges Arthur to see Glenalta; asks to be presented to Mrs. Douglas. P.S.: "Rome in the Nineteenth Century" by a female author.

**Letter X** – Miss Louisa Howard to Arthur, London. Mother ("la Madre", Mrs. Marianne Howard) - Uncle Mr. Ingoldsby of India House says ancient uncle (General Fred. Aubrey Douglas, "Nabob") coming home rich. Louisa suspects "new-light" religiosity. Adelaide to marry Viscount Crayton (Lord Crayton; "Lord C.", gambler). Lionel Strangeways, Sir Stephen, Annesley bores. Lady Anne Legrave, Lady Bilton (letter), Lady Penguin. Louisa's "ostracism" joke. Lord George; Lady Somerville's children; Lady Mildmay; Sir Hargrove Miles. Mother's arrangement with Crayton.

**Letter XI** – General Fred. Aubrey Douglas (Calcutta) to Mr. Otway. Returning, liver deranged, wants Hampshire/Staffordshire/Warwickshire estate £40–50,000; sends through Ingoldsby. Dislikes consanguinity; Henry (brother) married "absurd" marriage; General never answered Henry's letters. Asks about Mrs. H. Douglas.

## VOL. II (Letters XII–XXVI)

**Letter XII** – Otway to General Douglas (Lisfarne). Agrees to buy Marsden estate (Hampshire) from Sir Reginald Barnes via agent Mr. Snubb. Informs: eldest Douglas brother took name Howard (Mr. Howard died, left estate Buckinghamshire and house Grosvenor Square); Arthur heir. Mrs. Henry Douglas at Glenalta funded by legacy £20,000 from old Mrs. Norton. Lisfarne bought by Otway for Douglas family.

**Letter XIII** – Mrs. Eliza Sandford to Caroline Douglas (Checkley). Julia (17), Bertha (14 going on 15), Agnes (sick). Neighbours: Burleys (Sir Thomas, Lady B.), Henleys (strict sect; Priory), Liner, Peachum; Stanleys of Brandon Court (family of Mr. and Mrs. Stanley; Miss Stanleys called "blues"). Mr. Bentley (uncle of George) visits Checkley, sounds matchmaking; says Otway is an oddity; George "too close." Mr. Bentley fears Douglas girls will snare George; says money matters. Mrs. Sandford's wisdom on his "opportunity". Mentions George Bentley, Mount Prospect, Buxton.

**Letter XIV** – Arthur to Falkland (Glenalta, after Killarney plans). Russell (friend, smitten with Charlotte) and Annesley arrive unannounced (with Mrs. Fitzroy, Augusta). Mrs. Fitzroy: Englishwoman, Irish sympathies. Frederick back from exam (won gold medal; "Science Premium"). Ned of the Hill (Edmund Burke, hermit, Bible from pawn; "Wise Ned"); Frederick and Arthur visit him. Ned's opinions on education, Parliament, Emancipation, absentees. Arthur's ongoing adoption of Irish sympathies. Louisa's letter: Arthur should return; mother's ruse; Charlotte's music (Irish airs). Killarney excursion begins. Mrs. Fitzroy's coach. Arthur's grief.

**Letter XV** – Louisa Howard to Arthur. Mother has "horrible combustion"; Crayton's marriage to Adelaide is arranged; Lady Bilton's note; Duchess of Naresbury and Fancourt; Byron couplet; Crayton's gambling. Mrs. Burton anecdote (Pims).

**Letter XVI** – Mrs. Marianne Howard to Arthur (enclosed): asks him to come, raise money; Louisa's "blue" slip; General Douglas; "Lady Cantaloupe".

**Letter XVII** – Arthur to Louisa: refuses to act at wedding; fears Crayton's gambling and uncle's wealth; urges Louisa toward Douglas women.

**Letter XVIII** – Arthur to Falkland (Killarney). Party: Mrs. Fitzroy, Bentley senior, Russell, Annesley, Frederick, Emily, Charlotte, Fanny, Mr. Otway, Oliphant, Bentley junior. Boatman M'Carty More. Innisfallen; Oliphant on Irish antiquity (round towers, Persia). Bentley vs Mrs. Fitzroy ("Alexander no hero to his valet"; "pounded oyster shells"). Bentley on money matches; Oliphant on Mr. Bentley's youth (Miss Sharp rejection, lawyer Deeds & Co., inheritance); Otway's account. Lady Matilda Murray's party at Dinas Island; Miss Angelina Murray sermon jibe. Boat song "Who'll be King but Charley?"; Fanny: "Flora M'Donald". Russell proposes to Charlotte (rejected at Glena). Florence O'Neil drowned, widow fund. Fred made "king of Frederick's Island". Post-boy; sweep; illicit distillers. Arthur says Russell's proposal; Annesley's entail (Kepple, Compton). Louisa's letter recalls him; Mrs. Fitzroy's caleche.

**Letter XIX** – Louisa to Arthur (enclosed): mother forbids his coming; go abroad to join Falkland; wedding ruse; Lord Hawkston to give bride away.

**Letter XX** – (Letter from G. L. — "Clara Browne" narrative, to Otway, enclosed to Falkland). Clara Browne of Stockton; husband Mr. Browne; sisters Isabella (married Mr. Mills, universal showman) and Lavinia (married Mr. Dormer, inventor, absurd experiments); Adolphus (Clara's husband, sound judgment). Clara's moral: sense and temper over genius.

**Letter XXI** – Caroline to Elizabeth Sandford. Mrs. Fitzroy noticed Russell's feelings for Charlotte; Russell proposed in garden: Charlotte refused ("You and I have been educated in very different schools"). Annesley's departure. George Bentley described by Caroline (bookish, awkward; "moral atmosphere"). Caroline's poem "Sleep! balmy Sleep!". General Douglas's illness (India House letter).

**Letter XXII** – Arthur to Falkland (Glenalta, departure). Russell left; Charlotte calm. Moss-house gathering; Bentley's goose-verse ("Squire, dear, I live here"). Mrs. Fitzroy and Charlotte; Caroline's "Augusta" answer by Otway (Mrs. Fitzroy character analysis; "gold grain in sand"). Poet Connor (poet, verses). Mr. Fitzallan (liberal, pretended patriot) vs Ridley; Bentley's denunciation of Fitzallan; "Fort Ridley" vs "Rialta". Arthur's journey to Holyhead, Dublin. London: Louisa, the wedding of Adelaide and Crayton (quick, unceremonious), Crayton leaves for Dover/Continent. Uncle General expected. Arthur's debts.

**Letter XXIII** – Dr. A. Pancras to Mr. Otway (Limner's Hotel, London): General Douglas arrived, ill; asks Otway to come; Dr. Pancras accompanied from India.

**Letter XXIV** – Emily to Julia. Departure of Arthur and Mrs. Fitzroy; Frederick and Otway go to London; General arrived; Lord Crayton's Rome; Adelaide will be unhappy; Miss Talbot anecdote; Mortimer Fitzallan; Mr. Annesley and Russell contrasted.

**Letter XXV** – Frederick to his mother (London). Describes Aunt Howard (rouged, cold), Louisa (handsome, witty), London society; the "Lazy owls" passage; pensive young lady and statues; General Douglas tearful; Otway's company. Frederick's music skepticism.

**Letter XXVI** – Otway to Caroline. Praises Frederick ("le bel sauvage"; Macbeth lines "I have lived long enough", marked by General). Doctor Pancras; General to winter at Glenalta. General's character (Henry's line; "silver cords"). Otway's analysis of General's religious search.

## VOL. III (Letters XXVII–XLVI)

**Letter XXVII** – Frederick to Emily (London, last letter). Uncle's doctors; Frederick's distaste for London dinner with authors at Sir Marmaduke Liston's (Behemoth poet, metaphysician with toast-and-water, "Blue-stocking" gorgon). Arthur going to France.

**Letter XXVIII** – Arthur to Frederick (Paris). Adelaide; Louisa promises to avoid Lord G. Villiers; Arthur refuses to lend uncle money.

**Letter XXIX** – Caroline to Elizabeth Sandford. General's decline; wants to winter at Glenalta; Frederick's letter from Arthur revealed (misunderstanding resolved via Otway); Butler's Analogy read; General's conversion; the sea anemone image.

**Letter XXX** – Frederick to Arthur (Glenalta). Frederick graduated; plans for Turin; Oliphant to remain; Domine stays; "musical instrument" image of General.

**Letter XXXI** – Emily to Julia (Glenalta, last). Route to Marsden; Mr. Bentley's "Mount Prospect" name discussion with Mrs. Fitzroy; Domine's Birnam Wood reference; George Bentley's gentle nature; Crayton and Adelaide trouble.

**Letter XXXII** – Emily to Julia (Marsden). Hampshire election; Mr. Johnson (baronet's son); Mr. Bolton (old, witty) on Johnsons; "Oh" and "nice" as English words. Bolton on fashionable life.

**Letter XXXIII** – Otway to Oliphant (Marsden). Oliphant gets Glenalta parish (through General's promise). General's will: Marsden to Frederick, condition five years' residence; Frederick asks that Arthur be remembered; General leaves Arthur a sum to free estate.

**Letter XXXIV** – Caroline to Oliphant. Congratulates on preferment; her talk with General Douglas about Butler's Analogy and the soul's nature; General's objections (free will, identity). Fanny's "good Benefico."

**Letter XXXV** – Caroline to Otway (Marsden). Continues conversation with General: identity (Hunter, cannon, Napoleon hypothetical), free will, foreknowledge, Hooker quote "very best action requires to be forgiven." Tremaine critique (Dr. Evelyn). Caroline's regret at "modern" manners.

**Letter XXXVI** – Emily to Julia (Marsden). Mrs. Hannaper ("Jack Hannaper", masculine widow, election partisan; Miss Ormsby niece, Sir Christopher Cromie candidate). Hunting; Sir Archibald Johnson proposal; Mr. Bolton warns Hannaper; Campion archery party (Lady Campion, daughters, Lord Thornborough, Mrs. and Miss Fraser, midshipman); "Have you been out yet?"; bee; Lady Neville's party; Mr. Johnson asks to dance.

**Letter XXXVII** – Oliphant to Otway. Death of George Bentley's uncle Roger Bentley (Mount Prospect; fit; died in George's arms). Bentley's last words on Christian faith.

**Letter XXXVIII** – Otway to Oliphant. Shock; reflections on sending youth abroad; Emily refused Sir ?'s son's proposal (Baronet). Otway's letter contains reports.

**Letter XXXIX** – Emily to Julia (Brighton). Stanley (Alfred Stanley, clergyman) joins party; Sir Christopher Cromie's election; Mrs. Hannaper's £20,000 to niece; Lord Thornborough marries Lady Campion; Frederick's verses on Lady Gosling's ball.

**Letter XL** – Frederick to Oliphant (Paris). Louvre, Malmaison, Versailles; Lady Laura? Hints at George Bentley's proposal idea.

**Letter XLI** – Emily to Julia (Paris). Charles Falkland arrives with Arthur; Lord Crayton and Lady Crayton fled (Crayton killed Castelli in duel at Milan, fled; deep debts).

**Letter XLII** – Emily to Julia (Turin). Journey via Fontainebleau, Nivernois, Lyons, Mont Cenis; uncle declining.

**Letter XLIII** – Arthur to Frederick (Selby). Mother had paralytic stroke; Louisa; Dr. Leach; Mr. Arundel clergyman; Arthur refuses to leave England.

**Letter XLIV** – Frederick to Arthur (Turin). Excursion into Waldensian valleys (Pomaretto, Perosa, Pragella, La Torre, Angrogna); Falkland, Emily, Charlotte, Bentley, Otway; Stanley stays with General; Fanny with mother.

**Letter XLV** – Emily to Julia (Turin). Night shooting: Marchand (Lord Crayton, alias) shot himself; Adelaide (Lady Crayton) faints; Madame de Lisle (Lady Laura Penshurst, daughter of Earl of Alton) recognized by Otway; La Tour (maid) callous ("se consolera bientôt"). Arthur's mother died (letter to Frederick).

**Letter XLVI** – Arthur Howard to the Reader (final). Explains editing; Madame de Lisle's history; George Bentley settles in Angrogna (Waldensian valleys); Emily marries Charles Falkland (General gives £10,000); General dies in Frederick's arms (winter, Turin); Marsden sold; family return to Glenalta; Lawrence; Mrs. Fitzroy; Sandfords; Stanleys; Mr. Oliphant; Louisa and Mr. Stanley's brother; Frederick and Julia Sandford hinted; Mount Prospect renamed Cairndruid; Arthur's prefatory confession: "a sincere and penitent convert." Ends "THE END."

# Key names
Howard family: Arthur Howard (narrator), Mrs. Marianne Howard (mother), Louisa, Adelaide (m. Lord Crayton). Douglas family (Glenalta): Caroline Douglas (mother; widow of Henry Douglas), Frederick, Emily, Charlotte, Fanny. General Frederick Aubrey Douglas (uncle, Calcutta). Others: Edward "Phil." Otway (Lisfarne), Oliphant ("Domine"), Charles Falkland, Julia Sandford, Elizabeth Sandford (Checkley), George Bentley, Mr. Bentley senior, Mrs. Augusta Fitzroy, Russell, Annesley, Lewis (valet), Lawrence (old servant), Eileen, Tom Collins, Ned of the Hill, M'Carty More, Kate Sullivan, Mr. Bolton, Mrs. Hannaper, Lady Campion, Lord Thornborough, Alfred Stanley, Madame de Lisle (Lady Laura Penshurst).
